final.title: What folder structure hides in a small business
final.body:
For a small business owner, messy folders usually hide a simpler problem: repeated document search. If you keep hunting for customer agreements, invoices, contracts, or past decisions, the folder tree is not the workflow. It is where the friction shows up.

The bounded decision is not “reorganise everything.” It is: should the next automation effort start only after you can name one repeatable document task that matters, such as invoice filing, contract retrieval, or answering a customer query from old files? That is a threshold question, not a full system rebuild.

A practical next step is simple: pick your most common lookup for one week and note three things each time it happens. What were you looking for? Which folders did you check? How long did it take before you found it, or gave up and asked someone else? That is manual work, but it tells you whether the problem is occasional clutter or a recurring process worth automating.

If the same lookup keeps showing up and takes real time, you may have a workflow worth tightening. If it is ad hoc or takes seconds, the folder structure may be annoying, but not yet a business process. Folder names are often the smoke, not the fire.
